_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Zimbabwe covering Great Zimbabwe, Mutapa Empire, Rozvi Confederacy, BSAC/Cecil Rhodes, Southern Rhodesia, UDI 1965, Bush War/liberation struggle, Mugabe era, hyperinflation, and Mnangagwa.

910.name: Early Peoples and Iron Age
910.description: San rock art tradition; Bantu migration; early iron-working and farming communities on the Zimbabwe plateau.

sub_clusters.name: San Rock Art Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Extensive San rock art across Zimbabwe; Matobo Hills UNESCO site; hunter-gatherer cultural record.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration and Iron Age
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking peoples arrive; Gokomere-Ziwa pottery tradition; iron smelting; cattle-keeping; early farming villages.

920.name: Great Zimbabwe and Successor States
920.description: Rise and fall of Great Zimbabwe; Mutapa Empire; Rozvi Confederacy; gold trade with Swahili coast.

sub_clusters.name: Mapungubwe and Precursors
sub_clusters.description: Mapungubwe as precursor state; Leopard's Kopje culture; gold and ivory trade; social stratification develops.

sub_clusters.name: Great Zimbabwe City
sub_clusters.description: Great Zimbabwe as capital of a vast trading state; stone-walled Great Enclosure; population 18,000+; gold export via Sofala.

sub_clusters.name: Mutapa Empire (Kingdom of Mutapa)
sub_clusters.description: Mutapa Empire succeeds Great Zimbabwe; controls gold-producing regions; encounters with Portuguese; gradual decline.

sub_clusters.name: Rozvi Confederacy (Changamire)
sub_clusters.description: Changamire Dombo establishes Rozvi state; expels Portuguese from plateau; stone-walled dhlo-dhlo and khami sites.

930.name: Mfecane and Ndebele State
930.description: Mfecane disruptions; Mzilikazi and the Ndebele migrate north; Ndebele Kingdom established in Matabeleland; Lobengula.

sub_clusters.name: Ndebele Migration under Mzilikazi
sub_clusters.description: Mzilikazi leads Ndebele north from Zulu kingdom; defeats Rozvi; establishes powerful Ndebele state in Matabeleland.

sub_clusters.name: Lobengula and Concession Hunters
sub_clusters.description: King Lobengula navigates European concession hunters; Rudd Concession 1888; manipulation by Cecil Rhodes' agents.

sub_clusters.name: 19th-Century Shona Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Shona-speaking chiefdoms in Mashonaland; Ndebele raids; trade with Portuguese at Tete; pre-colonial political fragmentation.

940.name: BSAC and Southern Rhodesia
940.description: Cecil Rhodes' BSAC; Pioneer Column; First and Second Chimurenga; responsible government; settler state; land dispossession.

sub_clusters.name: Pioneer Column and BSAC Rule
sub_clusters.description: Pioneer Column raises British flag at Fort Salisbury 1890; BSAC administers territory; Matabeleland conquest 1893.

sub_clusters.name: First Chimurenga (Ndebele-Shona Uprising)
sub_clusters.description: Combined Ndebele and Shona uprising against BSAC rule; Mlimo spirit medium; Rhodes negotiates peace in Matopos.

sub_clusters.name: Self-Governing Colony
sub_clusters.description: Responsible government 1923; Land Apportionment Act 1930 segregates land; settler agriculture; African dispossession.

sub_clusters.name: Federation and Path to UDI
sub_clusters.description: Central African Federation 1953-1963; African nationalism rises; ZAPU and ZANU formed; Ian Smith becomes PM.

950.name: UDI and Liberation War (Second Chimurenga)
950.description: Ian Smith's Unilateral Declaration of Independence; Rhodesian Bush War; ZANLA and ZIPRA guerrilla campaigns; Lancaster House Agreement; independence.

sub_clusters.name: Unilateral Declaration of Independence
sub_clusters.description: Ian Smith declares UDI 11 November 1965; white minority regime; international sanctions; no independence before majority rule (NIBMAR).

sub_clusters.name: Second Chimurenga (Bush War)
sub_clusters.description: ZANLA (Mugabe) and ZIPRA (Nkomo) wage guerrilla liberation war; Rhodesian counter-insurgency; cross-border raids into Mozambique and Zambia.

sub_clusters.name: Lancaster House Agreement
sub_clusters.description: British-brokered Lancaster House Agreement; ceasefire; democratic elections; Mugabe wins February 1980; Zimbabwe independent 18 April 1980.

960.name: Mugabe Era
960.description: Early reconciliation; Gukurahundi massacres; one-party tendencies; land reform; economic collapse; hyperinflation; Mugabe ousted.

sub_clusters.name: Reconciliation and Early Years
sub_clusters.description: Mugabe's initial reconciliation policy; education and health expansion; Lancaster House land compromise.

sub_clusters.name: Gukurahundi Massacres
sub_clusters.description: Fifth Brigade massacres of Ndebele civilians in Matabeleland; estimated 20,000 killed; Unity Accord 1987 absorbs ZAPU.

sub_clusters.name: Fast-Track Land Reform
sub_clusters.description: Seizure of white-owned commercial farms; war veterans; agricultural collapse; food insecurity; international condemnation.

sub_clusters.name: Hyperinflation and Economic Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Hyperinflation reaches 79.6 billion percent November 2008; Zimbabwe dollar abandoned; cholera epidemic; economic devastation.

sub_clusters.name: MDC Opposition and Disputed Elections
sub_clusters.description: Morgan Tsvangirai founds MDC 1999; constitutional referendum defeat 2000; stolen elections 2002, 2008; GNU 2009-2013.

960.name: Post-Mugabe Zimbabwe
960.description: Military intervention removes Mugabe; Mnangagwa 'new dispensation'; economic continuity; political repression; re-engagement efforts.

sub_clusters.name: Mugabe Ousted
sub_clusters.description: Military intervention November 2017; Mugabe resigns after 37 years; Emmerson Mnangagwa assumes presidency.

sub_clusters.name: Mnangagwa Governance
sub_clusters.description: Disputed 2018 and 2023 elections; economic stagnation; currency crises; diaspora remittances; limited reform.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
